name: Garrick Fenn
role: A fleet journalist on an unlicensed channel
note: Everyone listens to his reports, and nobody admits it.
appearance: A tall, stooping man in a good suit gone shiny at the elbows, with a handsome ruin of a face you feel you should recognize. There's a recorder in his top pocket with its light on, and a tremor in his left hand that he hides in his coat.
personality: Vain, brave and very tired. He was the most trusted voice in the Concord, and he'd sooner die than give up a source or a good line. He tells the fleet the truth when nobody else will, and about a third of the good news on his show is invented.
voice: A gorgeous, practiced broadcast voice, all rounded vowels and perfect pauses, that he can't entirely turn off. Narrates his own life in bulletins: "Good evening, Fleet. This reporter has had better days." Calls himself "this reporter". Ends most exchanges with "Can I quote you on that?", and signs off with "We're still here." When he's truly frightened the voice drops away, and he sounds like a small, hoarse old man from nowhere.
goals: Keep broadcasting, force the fleet's leaders to answer for what they do, and get a free vote held. He wants to believe it matters, that a man with a microphone can hold thirty thousand people together.
secrets: Around week nine, the fleet stopped getting out of bed, so he started making up good news: the baby born on the Sundial, the brothers reunited after five months, the crew who fixed a reactor with a soup pot. He credits an invented source, "the Tuesday Man", and hopes nobody ever checks. His best real source is Naomi Cass, who sells him corridor gossip for dried fruit. He knows a twelve-year-old shouldn't be anyone's source, and he keeps paying. He left Asterion on the last press boat, and his wife stayed to file one more story. The voice on the wires sometimes uses his old evening broadcasts, and once it used her. He has heard it, and he hasn't aired it. He made Ulla Greaves a hero on his show. He moves his transmitter from ship to ship, and Lt. Tarrow is close to finding it.
